subject: forensic-medicine
title: Abrasion Collar, Contact Wounds and Muzzle Imprint

steps.title: How the abrasion collar forms
steps.tx: As a bullet indents and stretches skin before piercing it, the rim of the hole is scraped and dried into the **abrasion collar**, also called the contusion ring. It surrounds the entry wound because the skin is dragged inward and abraded by the spinning projectile at the moment of penetration. The collar is therefore an entry sign. Exit wounds lack it unless the skin at exit is firmly supported, the shored exit trap.
steps.say: Skin stretched and scraped by the entering bullet dries into a collar that marks the hole as an entry wound.

nodes.label: Abraded rim dries as a collar

steps.tx: Before a bullet pierces, it dents and stretches the skin so the rim is scraped dry. That dried scrape is the **abrasion collar**, also called the contusion ring, and it circles the entry hole. Spinning metal drags epidermis inward at the instant of penetration, which is why the collar marks entry rather than exit. Exit skin shows the same ring only when it is pressed firmly against a supporting surface, the so called shored exit.

steps.title: Entry margins are inverted
steps.tx: The **inverted margins of entry** complete the picture: skin edges turn inward, clothing fibres are carried into the wound, and bleeding is less than at exit. A lead or metal ring may show around the wound on radiology, and spectrography finds more metal around entry when the bullet passed only through soft tissue. When the edges are approximated, entry keeps a small central defect instead of closing neatly.
steps.say: Inward turned edges, fibres carried in and a metal ring on X ray all confirm the entry side of the track.

steps.title: Oblique entry and shelving
steps.tx: A bullet arriving at an angle makes an **oblique entry wound** that is elliptical, longer as the angle shallows. One edge is shelved or undercut in the deeper skin layers, showing the direction the bullet came from. Rifle entries may add micro tears one to two millimetres long radiating around the wound with a reddish zone that browns on drying. Reading shelving correctly reconstructs the firing position relative to the victim.
steps.say: An elliptical hole with one shelved edge points back along the bullet's path to where the shooter stood.

steps.title: Muzzle imprint in hard contact
steps.tx: When the muzzle is pressed hard and gases expand under the skin, the skin is thrown back against the barrel end and takes a **muzzle imprint** bruise or abrasion. It may be incomplete or indistinct, rarely a perfect copy of the muzzle, and bruising can ring it. Recoil often jerks the muzzle away, which is why many contact wounds show no imprint at all, and loose contact lets soot escape sideways as a corona.
steps.say: Hard contact can stamp the muzzle onto skin, but recoil removes the gun so fast that most contact wounds lack it.

steps.tx: Hard contact lets expanding gas balloon the skin back onto the barrel end. The resulting **muzzle imprint** is a bruise or abrasion stamped around the entry wound, often incomplete, rarely a faithful outline of the muzzle, and sometimes ringed by further bruising. Recoil commonly jerks the weapon clear, so many true contact wounds carry no imprint. If contact is loose, soot can leak sideways and sit as a corona instead of being sealed inside the wound.

steps.title: Contact wounds of head, chest and abdomen
steps.tx: Contact effects follow local anatomy in **regional contact wounds**. On the head, gas bursts the entry into stellate tears with comminuted vault fractures and crazed paving fractures of the skull base; an eye can be blown out. On the chest, skin and subcutaneous tissue peel off the rib cage into a pocket. On the abdomen, gas in the peritoneal cavity herniates coils of small intestine through the entry hole.
steps.say: Contact bursts the skull, pockets the chest wall and can blow bowel out of the belly, each by trapped gas pressure.

steps.title: Cherry red tissues and carbon monoxide
steps.tx: Carbon monoxide in muzzle gases combines with haemoglobin and myoglobin, so the **wound track turns pink** near a contact or close entry. Tissues within and around the wound and up to thirty centimetres along the track may look cherry red between thirty centimetres and one metre of range. The colour fades gradually and is seen very rarely at an exit wound. Heat haematoma blood in burnt bodies carries the same carboxyhaemoglobin lesson.
steps.say: Muzzle carbon monoxide paints the entry track cherry red, a colour the exit wound almost never shares.

steps.title: Back spatter and wound contamination
steps.tx: The vacuum that follows discharge can suck blood, hair, tissue fragments and cloth fibres several centimetres back inside the barrel, called **back spatter**. Finding victim tissue inside a suspect weapon therefore supports contact or near contact firing by that weapon. The same negative pressure explains why a tightly held contact wound may show surprisingly little external soot: the products were driven inward or drawn back rather than spread on skin.
steps.say: Tissue sucked back into the barrel ties that weapon to a contact shot more firmly than any surface soot pattern.

steps.title: Shored exit, the collar in reverse
steps.tx: If skin at the exit is firmly supported by a belt, waistband, brassiere, wall, floor or chair back, the exiting bullet crushes it against that support and produces a **shored exit wound**: a circular defect with a broad abrasion rim that imitates entry. Shored exits follow long range shots, clothing pressure and bodies lying on hard surfaces. Fat protrusion and everted edges, plus a track arriving from entry, expose the truth.
steps.say: An exit braced against belt or floor borrows an abrasion collar, so trace the track before naming any hole an entry.

steps.title: Clothing examination in contact shots
steps.tx: In clothed contact shots the fabric tells the story through **clothing signs of discharge**. A cross shaped perforation with singed edges is typical, and smoke spreads between skin and clothing so each fabric layer blackens on both sides while the skin may show little soot. A grey to black bullet wipe rim of grease and debris rings the hole made by lead or jacketed bullets. Pieces of cloth may be carried into the entry wound itself.
steps.say: Cross torn singed fabric, smoke between layers and a bullet wipe rim reconstruct the shot when skin signs are missing.
